samples.summary: Clipboard sanitizer drops `colSpan: 0` covered-cell markers, breaking merged tables on internal paste
samples.evidence:
`sanitizeCell` only keeps a span when it is `> 1`:
```
if (colSpan !== undefined && colSpan > 1) cell.colSpan = Math.trunc(colSpan);
```
But `colSpan: 0` is the *covered-cell marker* the layout relies on — `normalizeTableMerges` (model/types.ts:592) writes `cell.colSpan = 0` for every cell an anchor covers (including rowSpan coverage), and `computeTableLayout` (view/table-layout.ts:158-164) skips a cell only when `colSpan === 0`. Before this change the payload's cells were passed through verbatim, so the markers survived a copy/paste.

The cell-range paste path self-heals (`pasteTableCells` calls `normalizeTableMerges`, text-editor.ts:3708/3740), but the whole-table-block paste path does **not**: `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3565-3584) inserts `cloneBlockWithFreshIds(blocks[0])` with no normalization. So copying a table that contains merged cells and pasting it back produces a table whose merges are gone — the previously covered cells render as real cells with their own width, and any anchor keeps `colSpan > 1`, violating the invariant the layout documents it trusts.

samples.summary: `columnWidths` fallback of `100` is in the wrong unit — column widths are ratios, not pixels
samples.evidence:
`for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 100);`

`TableData.columnWidths` holds *fractions*: `createTableBlock` fills `Array(cols).fill(1 / cols)` (model/types.ts:542), the DOCX importer divides by `totalWidth` (import/docx-importer.ts:277), and the layout does `columnWidths.map(ratio => ratio * contentWidth)` (view/table-layout.ts:140). A fallback of `100` therefore yields a column 100× the content width whenever an entry is missing or non-numeric (a truncated or hostile payload, or a row that has more cells than the payload has widths). The correct default is `1 / cols`.

samples.summary: Column count derived from row cell counts truncates `columnWidths`; `rowHeights` re-indexed against dropped rows
samples.evidence:
`const cols = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.cells.length));` then `columnWidths` is rebuilt with exactly `cols` entries, discarding any further widths from the payload. `numCols = columnWidths.length` (table-layout.ts:136) is the authoritative column count, so any row that carries more cells than `cols` — or the source table's real column count when a row is dropped — silently loses trailing columns (their cells are never laid out).
Similarly `table.rowHeights = rows.map((_, r) => asNumber((value.rowHeights as unknown[])[r]))` indexes the raw heights by the *sanitized* row index; rows skipped at line 261 shift every subsequent height onto the wrong row.

samples.summary: Clamping the DOCX heading level to 6 demotes legitimately imported Heading 7–9 paragraphs
samples.evidence:
`const level = Math.min(6, Math.max(1, Math.trunc(Number(headingLevel)) || 1));`

The importer can legitimately produce levels above 6: `docx-style-map.ts:139` does `headingLevel = parseInt(headingMatch[1], 10)` from Word's `Heading N` style, and `model/named-styles.ts:106-108` documents exactly this ("DOCX import reads `Heading N` from Word where N can be 7–9"), clamping only for *style-id* lookup. Word defines Heading7–Heading9, so the previous `Heading${headingLevel}` round-tripped them faithfully; the new clamp rewrites them as `Heading6`, silently changing the document on import→export. Sanitizing the value is right, but the ceiling should be 9 (or the level should be clamped where the block model is written, not at export).

samples.summary: `foldedHeadingLevel` strips a real heading destination's level when a bullet is pasted into it
samples.evidence:
`if (destOwnTextLen > 0) { return dest.type === 'list-item' ? dest.headingLevel : undefined; }`

When the caret sits inside a real `heading` block that keeps its own text and the pasted head/tail block is a `list-item`, the destination becomes a list-item with **no** remembered level, so the heading's own provenance is destroyed by a paste that never touched it — the exact failure mode the doc comment says the function exists to prevent ("a destination that keeps its own text keeps its *own* memory"). Returning `dest.headingLevel` for a `heading` destination too would be consistent. (Behaviour matches the pre-change code, so this is a missed case rather than a new regression.)

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` trusts `headingLevel` on any block, including out-of-range levels written by the DOCX importer
samples.evidence:
`if (block.headingLevel !== undefined) return { type: 'heading', opts: { headingLevel: block.headingLevel } };`

`import/docx-importer.ts:242` writes `block.headingLevel = headingLevel as Block['headingLevel']` for *any* paragraph whose style resolves to `Heading N` — including a numbered (`list-item`) paragraph and including N = 7–9 (see `named-styles.ts:106`). Un-bulleting such an imported list item therefore calls `setBlockType(id, 'heading', { headingLevel: 7 })`, storing a value outside the declared `HeadingLevel` union. Nothing crashes (`blockStyleId` clamps, and the export clamp above now clamps too), but the invalid level is persisted into the CRDT and the type declaration is violated.

finding.summary: Clipboard sanitizer drops `colSpan: 0` covered-cell markers, breaking merged tables on internal paste
finding.evidence:
`sanitizeCell` only keeps a span when it is `> 1`:
```
if (colSpan !== undefined && colSpan > 1) cell.colSpan = Math.trunc(colSpan);
```
But `colSpan: 0` is the *covered-cell marker* the layout relies on — `normalizeTableMerges` (model/types.ts:592) writes `cell.colSpan = 0` for every cell an anchor covers (including rowSpan coverage), and `computeTableLayout` (view/table-layout.ts:158-164) skips a cell only when `colSpan === 0`. Before this change the payload's cells were passed through verbatim, so the markers survived a copy/paste.

The cell-range paste path self-heals (`pasteTableCells` calls `normalizeTableMerges`, text-editor.ts:3708/3740), but the whole-table-block paste path does **not**: `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3565-3584) inserts `cloneBlockWithFreshIds(blocks[0])` with no normalization. verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim: clipboard.ts:238-241 keeps colSpan/rowSpan only when >1, discarding the `colSpan: 0` covered-cell marker. That marker is the sole coverage signal the layout trusts (table-layout.ts:157-164 skips a cell only on `colSpan === 0`; types.ts:564-565,592 documents/writes it). Copy preserves the marker (text-editor.ts:3451 uses `!= null`), so a round-trip through serializeClipboard/deserializeClipboard strips coverage while leaving the anchor's colSpan>1. The whole-table-block paste path has no repair: handlePaste (text-editor.ts:1242,1254) -> insertBlocks (3565-3584) inserts cloneBlockWithFreshIds with no normalization, and a repo-wide grep shows normalizeTableMerges is called only at text-editor.ts:3708/3740 inside pasteTableCells (the cell-range path). Result is a broken documented invariant and visually corrupted merged tables on a real user path — a correctness/state-corruption bug in this lens.

finding.summary: `columnWidths` fallback of `100` is in the wrong unit — column widths are ratios, not pixels
finding.evidence:
`for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 100);`

`TableData.columnWidths` holds *fractions*: `createTableBlock` fills `Array(cols).fill(1 / cols)` (model/types.ts:542), the DOCX importer divides by `totalWidth` (import/docx-importer.ts:277), and the layout does `columnWidths.map(ratio => ratio * contentWidth)` (view/table-layout.ts:140). A fallback of `100` therefore yields a column 100× the content width whenever an entry is missing or non-numeric (a truncated or hostile payload, or a row that has more cells than the payload has widths). The correct default is `1 / cols`.

verdict.reason: The quoted line is present verbatim at packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:268 (`columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 100)`). TableData.columnWidths is unambiguously a set of fractions: createTableBlock fills `1 / cols` (model/types.ts:542), document.ts renormalizes to `1 / count` on insert/delete columns (model/document.ts:665-668, 701-703), the DOCX importer divides by totalWidth (import/docx-importer.ts:277), and the layout comment plus code convert ratios to pixels via `ratio * contentWidth` (view/table-layout.ts:139-140). A fallback of 100 therefore yields a column 100x the content width and blows up cumulative x-offsets (table-layout.ts:145-148). No downstream guard normalizes it: normalizeTableMerges (model/types.ts:574-620), the only repair pass invoked on pasted tables (view/text-editor.ts:3708, 3740), only fixes colSpan/rowSpan. The path is reachable: asNumber rejects non-finite/non-number values (clipboard.ts:69-71) so the fallback fires for missing/NaN/string entries or an absent columnWidths array (rawWidths = [] at line 266), and `cols` is derived from max row cell count (line 265) independent of the widths array length; the file's own header (lines 36-43) documents this payload as attacker-writable, entering via deserializeBlocks (line 26) and deserializeClipboard (line 354). Correct default is 1 / cols. Real, unguarded correctness/unit bug.

finding.summary: Enter at offset 0 of a bulleted heading strands the remembered level on the empty leading bullet; the heading's text loses it (asymmetric with a plain heading)
finding.evidence: In `Doc.splitBlock`, a `list-item` always yields `newType = 'list-item'` (line 330), and `applySplitBlock` deletes `after.headingLevel` whenever `newBlockType !== 'heading'` (block-helpers.ts:256). So splitting a bulleted heading at offset 0 gives: `before` = empty list-item that KEEPS `headingLevel`, `after` = list-item holding the entire original heading text with NO `headingLevel`. Un-bulleting the text then produces a plain paragraph — exactly the Heading-2-downgrade the change set out to fix. The plain-heading path is deliberately not asymmetric: for `type === 'heading'` with `offset < blockText.length` the new block is also a `heading` (lines 332-337), so real headings survive an Enter at offset 0. The Yorkie store has the same asymmetry (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2140 only copies the level when `newBlockType === 'heading'`). The new tests only cover splitting at the END of the text (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts 'splitting a bulleted heading leaves the new bullet plain'), so offset 0 is unguarded.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence is factually absent. `applySplitBlock` does NOT delete `after.headingLevel` whenever `newBlockType !== 'heading'`: block-helpers.ts:260 computes `movesMemory = splitMovesHeadingMemory(block, offset, newBlockType)`, line 261 guards the delete with `&& !movesMemory`, and lines 264-266 strip `before.headingLevel` instead. `splitMovesHeadingMemory` (block-helpers.ts:290-302) fires exactly for offset===0 on a non-empty list-item that has a remembered headingLevel splitting into a list-item — i.e. precisely the scenario alleged to be unguarded, and it moves the level onto the half holding the text. The Yorkie path is not asymmetric either: yorkie-doc-store.ts:2017 calls the same shared helper, 2027-2031 removes the attribute from the original tree node, and 2062-2067 / 2155-2158 copy it onto the new block via `(newBlockType === 'heading' || movesHeadingMemory)`. The cited yorkie-doc-store.ts:2140 is inside the empty-inline cleanup loop, not a headingLevel copy. Coverage claim is also wrong: list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:230-253 tests the offset-0 split explicitly and asserts first.headingLevel undefined / second.headingLevel === 2 and the resulting unlistedBlockType outcomes. Additionally document.ts:303-307 diverts empty bulleted list-items before the split, so no other offset-0 list-item path reaches the delete unguarded.

finding.summary: Multi-block paste into an empty bulleted list item collapses head and tail into the same block, scrambling the pasted content
finding.evidence: `insertBlocks` multi-block branch does `const tailBlockId = this.docSplitBlock(pos.blockId, pos.offset)` (line 3596) and then treats `pos.blockId` as the head and `tailBlockId` as a distinct tail. But `Doc.splitBlock` short-circuits for an empty list item — `if (block.type === 'list-item' && blockText.length === 0) { setBlockType(...); return blockId; }` (document.ts:303-307, a branch this diff edits) — returning the SAME id, so `tailBlockId === pos.blockId`. The head write (lines 3603-3610) appends `firstPasted`'s inlines, middle blocks are inserted after it (3621-3625), and then lines 3628-3640 re-read that same block as `tailBlock` and splice `lastPasted` at offset 0, producing `lastPasted + firstPasted` in one block with the middle blocks after it, plus type/style/headingLevel taken from `lastPasted`. The new test only covers a SINGLE-block paste into an emptied bulleted heading, so this path is untested. (Pre-existing, but the empty-list-item exit branch is directly modified here and the new `headingLevel` bookkeeping runs through it.)

verdict.reason: The finding claims insertBlocks' multi-block branch unconditionally calls `this.docSplitBlock(pos.blockId, pos.offset)`, so an empty list item makes Doc.splitBlock short-circuit and return the same id, collapsing head and tail. That code is not present. text-editor.ts:3614-3627 explicitly tests `destBlock.type === 'list-item' && getBlockTextLength(destBlock) === 0` (`splitExitsList`) and, when true, creates a fresh paragraph via `createBlock('paragraph')`, inserts it with `insertBlockAfter`, performs the same `pending?.rebindAnchor` that docSplitBlock does (403-407), and uses that new id as `tailBlockId`; `docSplitBlock` is only called in the else branch (3626). The guard condition is exactly equivalent to the short-circuit it protects against: Doc.splitBlock short-circuits on `block.type === 'list-item' && getBlockText(block).length === 0` (document.ts:303-307), and getBlockText(b).length and getBlockTextLength(b) both fold over block.inlines summing inline.text lengths (model/types.ts:349-358). So tailBlockId can never equal pos.blockId on that path, and the head write (3630-3642) and tail write (3660-3673) always target distinct blocks — no interleaving of lastPasted before firstPasted. The in-code comment at 3609-3613 names this exact hazard as the reason the branch exists. The remaining substance of the finding (no multi-block test for this path) is test coverage, which is outside the correctness lens.
